title: The forge seam is read-only: the harness never changes anything on a code host
Providers drive the operator-installed gh and glab; the harness holds no forge token
A code host is contacted only after the user enabled the entry, only for a listed host, and only while someone is looking
Bindings are explicit log events written when a shell call settles
client-ui-forge becomes three server-rendered surfaces; the code-review client is dropped
A worktree move never widens what a session may write; the Git directory grant is retained, not added
The log says who owns a worktree, a journal covers each operation in flight, and cleanup removes only clean, unreferenced checkouts
Worktrees are created explicitly: before the first turn, by the tool, or for a delegated child that asked for isolation; no message is held and no subagent is isolated automatically
What a status read does not cover is deferred, with what would reopen each
ForChild creates a worktree as an effect of a child's activation, cleans up on disposal and failure, and never moves a live session
A session can move into its own checkout and branch, and back, by a host operation or by two model tools
A worktree is cleaned up when its session goes away, and a crash leaves a named remainder
Change-request status is read through one provider-neutral registry with shared, bounded polling
GitHub and GitLab status providers that run the user's own command-line tool
A session lists the change requests it works on, across resume and fork
The user sees checkout and change-request status beside the conversation and can start a session in a worktree
Worktree creation from every revision form refuses existing names, copies no dirty files and runs no repository-configured program
Every Git start carries the session's policy, is never retried unconfined, and the Git directory grant is retained only when it was inside the roots
Worktree tool schemas and results; a tool moves only through SetForCall, inside the anchor and the write roots; no sequence of enter and exit widens the root
A failure after each creation step rolls back exactly that operation's artifacts, or leaves an uncertain journal row
Cleanup on archive and delete removes only clean owned checkouts, keeps branches, and marks a dead instance's rows uncertain once
A failed worktree attempt from the UI blocks step 1 with its reason and no model request
Forge polling cadence, backoff, no call without a watcher, stored snapshots after a restart, and no mutating provider method
Both providers against a scripted command-line tool: snapshots, partial errors, failure codes and a credential-free child environment
Remote and change-request address parsing for both providers; an unlisted host starts no process
Binding events from command lines and outputs, including shortened results, and their replay, fork, dismiss and track
Golden panel fragments in English and Chinese, escaped code-host text, and owner-only mutations
With the bundles disabled, or enabled with no tab open, no gh, glab or Git process starts
Two sessions work in parallel in their own worktrees and both can commit under a real sandbox
Cleanup on archive and delete, and a host killed mid-operation, against real Git
A session's pull request and merge request appear with live status, using only the user's CLI sign-in
Starting a session in a worktree from a real browser, including a failed attempt

reason: Upstream's largest client package (1.37 MB of source: a host Remote plus a React client) becomes one Go component that renders three fragments on the host: a session-panel section with checkout and change-request cards, a worktree control with its card, and a session-list glyph. Its changes view, review threads and writes, Code review page and lens extension interface are dropped by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-5; its merge and other host actions by DH-ADR-XFORGE-1.

The provider registry and shared polling loop are kept with upstream's cadence, backoff and one-fetch-per-family rule, as component x.forge under forge.Key. The provider interface shrinks from 27 operations to six reads and a description, because the harness never writes to a code host; the last snapshot per change request is now stored.

The bundle is seven configuration rows and an icon. In Go it is an optional bundle file, x.forge, holding one disabled group, beside a separate x.worktree bundle, so the two no longer collide when both are selected; enabling the group is the user's opt-in to contacting the listed hosts.

The GitHub provider keeps upstream's mechanism: it runs the operator-installed gh on the host and holds no token. It is started through the one process starter instead of execa, and is reduced to status reads, head lookup, readiness and address mapping; diff, commit, review, viewed-mark and write operations are not built.

The GitLab provider keeps running the operator-installed glab on the host with the redirecting variables removed and a scratch working directory, including the batch halving when GitLab refuses a query as too complex. It is reduced to the same read-only operations as the GitHub provider.

Bindings of change requests to sessions are kept, with track, dismiss, branch discovery and session watches under bind.Key. The mechanism changes: a listener writes an explicit forge/binding event when a shell call settles, and the fold reads only those events, where upstream re-parses tool text on every fold.

The two model tools are kept as component x.worktree.tools, separate from the service so that an agent preset without them pays no prompt tokens. They move a session only through workdir.Service.SetForCall, which the working-directory owner (DH-ADR-VIEW-8) limits to the anchor; in addition a target must lie inside the session's current write roots and exit returns to the directory the session entered from.

The worktree service is kept as component x.worktree under worktree.Key: create, enter, exit and restore run Git under the session's own policy and move the session through the working-directory service. Added: rollback of a failed attempt, a journal of operations in flight, cleanup on deletion as well as archive, and a retained grant to the common Git directory. Dropped: the Node helper process.

The local-changes count is still computed with Git's clean and process filters skipped, so a materialised LFS file can count as changed. The part about Git older than 2.31 ignoring the overrides is removed: the worktree and inspection code refuses such a Git.
justification: Running repository-configured filter programs during a background refresh would execute repository code on every tool result. The count is labelled as computed with filters skipped when filter drivers are configured, and the diff viewer that showed the misleading lines is not built.

reason: The limit concerns scopes of the changes view (a missing last-turn scope and the Branch scope's default base). The changes view is not built; per-turn file changes are shown by the filesystem area's workspace-changes card.

Upstream reads every ref and filters in the host. The Go base-branch search passes the query to git for-each-ref as a pattern with a count, sorted by commit date, so Git filters and bounds the list and nothing reads every ref.
The limit is that a patch over the size ceiling shows no files and long lines are cut in the side-by-side view. No diff is read or drawn in the Go design; the card links to the code host's page.

The limit describes syntax colouring across collapsed lines in the React changes view, a consequence of highlighting in the browser as file sections draw. It exists only because of that client rendering, and the view is not built (DH-ADR-XFORGE-5).

The limit describes placeholder heights of file sections that React has not drawn yet, a consequence of the client's lazy rendering. It exists only because of that client rendering, and the view is not built (DH-ADR-XFORGE-5).
The limit says the browser's find-in-page misses lines the React view has not drawn. It exists only because of that client's lazy rendering, and the view is not built (DH-ADR-XFORGE-5).
The limit concerns viewed marks kept on the code host or in one browser. Viewed marks are not built: the harness neither reads nor writes them, and nothing is kept in browser storage for them.

The limit concerns review-thread writes, the pending review and avatars loaded from the code host's image server. The harness writes nothing to a code host, shows no review threads, and loads no image from another origin.

The limit concerns the lens and annotation extension interface of the changes view. It is a client-plugin extension point with no place in a server-rendered UI, and it is not built together with the view it extends.
The limit concerns review layers (Interface, Implementation, Tests) derived from path rules and .gitattributes. Review layers are a feature of the changes view, which is not built.

Status is still polled only while a browser tab shows that session's panel, and no notification is raised for checks that finish meanwhile. Changed: session-list rows start no polling at all and show the stored status with its time.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-3: polling with no viewer would contact the user's code host in the background and spend the user's rate limit with nobody to show the result to. Browser notifications belong to the web application area.

reason: The limit concerns choosing commits of a change request or branch in the changes view. Commit selection is not built, and the provider operations that listed and compared commits are removed with it.

The limit lists gaps of the Code review page (GitHub-only lists, no host or account choice, a staged binding lost on restart). The page is not built; reviewing a change request the session does not own is done on the code host.

Upstream's list reads worktree and bindings of an unloaded session from a cache that may be missing. In Go both are summary folds registered with the session-views area, whose checkpoints commit in the same transaction as their events and are caught up for any session, so no session lacks them.

A change made outside the session to unstaged files still appears only at the next trigger: a tool result, a panel fetch or a refresh, throttled to once per 10 seconds. Narrowed: a watch on the Git directory's HEAD file makes a commit or a branch switch made outside appear promptly.
justification: Watching a whole working tree for the panel would cost one watch per directory of every open session's repository. The panel is a status summary, and the triggers plus the HEAD watch cover the changes that alter what it shows.

reason: Upstream leaves a branch or checkout behind after a failed or cancelled attempt. In Go a journal row is written before the first Git command and a failed attempt rolls back what that row created: the registration and directory by a non-force removal, the branch only if it still points at the pinned base commit. Generated names still come from the session id, which is a naming rule and not a defect.

Upstream's hold misses a message that arrives during a turn or other maintenance. The Go design has no hold: creation from the UI is its own operation offered only before the first turn, a message sent meanwhile is latched by the driver, and a failed attempt blocks step 1 through a PreStep listener. Not falling back silently when a worktree was removed by hand needs the session-views area to route recovery through workdir.Access (open question 1b).

Upstream keeps the agent idle in maintenance with no stop control while a message waits for a failed creation. In Go nothing waits: a failed attempt ends the maintenance task, the turn ends as blocked with the reason, and the composer stays usable.

Restoring a worktree whose directory was removed still recreates it from the branch, or from the base commit when the branch is gone, and changes that were never committed are lost. An existing or incomplete directory still blocks the restore.
justification: Git holds only what was committed, so nothing can bring back files that existed only in the removed directory. The card says so before the user chooses Restore, and the restore never overwrites an existing directory.

reason: Upstream disables the option when the project is itself a linked worktree, because its Git directory lies outside the writable root, and Windows ignored extra roots. In Go the worktree component retains a grant to the common Git directory when it was inside the session's roots and otherwise asks the user for a directory session grant; the sandbox area gives every write root its own identifier on Windows (its decision DH-ADR-SANDBOX-6).

Upstream needs a profile patch file to add a GitHub Enterprise or self-managed GitLab host. In Go hosts is an ordinary field of each provider's config struct, shown on the settings form derived from the type and saved to the one writable layer.
The model still has no tool for bound change requests. It reads and changes them with gh and glab through the shell tool.
justification: A host-side tool would read with the user's own sign-in outside the session's sandbox and network policy, and a session can bind any address by naming it in a command, so such a tool needs its own approval rule. That design is deferred until the feature leaves experimental; the shell route is already guarded.

reason: gh must still be installed and signed in for each listed host, tokens in environment variables are still not forwarded, and an unlisted host is never read. Without gh the cards report unavailable with the reason, and sign-out shows the sign-in command.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-2: the vendor's tool owns token storage, sign-in and refresh, so the harness holds no forge credential. This matches outcome DH-O-10 for capabilities whose provider is operator-installed software.

reason: A status read still counts at most maxReviewThreads review threads per pull request and reports a lower bound beyond that, shown as N+. The review read the bullet also mentions is not built.
justification: GitHub offers no count of unresolved threads, so the provider must page through them, and an unbounded page loop would let one pull request exhaust the user's rate limit. The bound is configuration and the card marks a truncated count.

reason: Upstream reads continuation pages inside the host's polling batch, so one pull request with many threads can time out the whole batch. In Go the batch returns each pull request's first page, and continuation pages are read per pull request with their own deadline, so a slow one fails alone.
The limit concerns the merge base of a diff read from GitHub after the base branch was rewritten. The Go provider reads no diff from the code host.
A head lookup still excludes pull requests whose head branch is in another repository, so a pull request opened elsewhere from a fork is not discovered by branch name.
justification: A pull request the session creates from a fork still binds from the address the create command prints. Discovering others needs a lookup of the fork's parent on every push, and a branch name in a fork can collide with someone else's pull request; this is deferred, with Add by link as the manual route.

reason: Every poll still costs one GraphQL query per host plus one per further page of threads, counted against the signed-in account. Removed: the queries for diffs, review reads and review writes, which are not built.
justification: Status is read by polling and polling costs requests; there is no webhook intake. The cost is bounded by polling only while a panel is shown, by upstream's cadence, and by backing off until the reset time on a rate-limited answer.

reason: The limit is that the provider never joins a merge queue. The Go provider never merges at all; merging is done on the code host or by the model's own command.
glab must still be installed and signed in for each listed host, an unlisted host is never read, and a host whose SSH remotes use another name or a GitLab under a path prefix is still not recognised.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-2, for the same reason as the GitHub provider: the harness holds no forge credential. Recognising hosts by anything but the listed host names would guess at where credentials may be sent.

reason: The limit is that the GitLab provider keeps no viewed marks, so the view keeps them in the browser. Viewed marks are not built for any provider.
The limit is a rebase request sent without a head check. The Go provider sends no rebase or any other write.

The limit is a mismatch between the unresolved count, which includes overview discussions, and the thread list, which omits them. The Go design shows only the count the host reports and has no thread list, so the two cannot disagree.
The limit concerns comment authors never marked as bots and draft notes carrying the read's time. Comments and draft notes are not read or shown.
The status query still reads only fields that GitLab Community Edition has; required approvals, code owners and merged-results pipelines of paid tiers are not read.
justification: A query naming a paid-tier field is refused by a Community Edition host, so reading those fields needs a capability probe per host and a second query shape. That is deferred; the card shows what every edition reports.

reason: Every poll still costs one GraphQL query per batch plus one REST request per merge request whose mergeability must be rechecked. Removed: the requests for review reads, diff versions, draft notes and writes, which are not built.
justification: Status is read by polling, as for the GitHub provider, and GitLab rechecks mergeability only when a REST read asks. The cost is bounded by polling only while a panel is shown and by the configured batch size and concurrency.

reason: Only command-line tools with a compiled-in rule bind; expansions, substitutions, multi-line scripts, undeclared options and aliases are still excluded. Tightened: a numeric selector without a literal repository no longer binds, because upstream's live lookup is not built.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-4: the reader never guesses and never executes anything, so a binding is always a fact. Misses are recovered by branch discovery after a push or on inspection, and by Add by link in the panel.

reason: Upstream hashes the registered rule set into the fold's state version, so a new or changed rule refolds every session and a start without a provider removes its bindings. In Go the fold reads only forge/binding events and never consults a rule; rules are compiled-in data used once, when a command settles.
A change request opened elsewhere for a branch still appears only after the next push of that branch, the next inspection that reports the branch, or a manual add.
justification: There is no webhook intake in this area, so the harness learns of a change request only when it looks. The registry's Refresh and the binding service's DiscoverBranch are the entries a webhook component would call; building that component belongs to the webhook area.

reason: The model still cannot read or change bindings through a tool.
justification: Same reason as forge-bundle.2: a host-side forge tool would act with the user's sign-in outside the session's sandbox and network policy and needs its own approval rule, which is deferred until the feature leaves experimental.

reason: A command run in the background still contributes binding evidence only from the result its call returned; later job output adds none.
justification: The observer reads settled tool calls, and whether a background job's final output is delivered as a settled outcome is for the execution and jobs areas to define. Until then a change request created in the background is found by branch discovery at the next inspection, or added by link.

reason: Upstream treats a tag printed without refs/tags/ as a branch and may bind a change request of the same name. In Go the live discovery step asks Git whether refs/heads/<name> exists in the session's checkout and skips a name that is only a tag.

Upstream binds a program's shell call from the logged copy of its output, which the spill policy can shorten. In Go the observer reads the complete output when the call settles, through the spill store when the result was shortened, up to maxScanBytes, and records what it found as an event, so replay does not depend on the shortened text.

Upstream shows a parent session none of its subagents' bindings. In Go the panel lists the bindings of the session's subagent children as well, each labelled with the child, read from the children's summary folds.
Upstream writes lookup failures to the host log only. In Go a failed discovery is kept in the panel state for that branch with its failure code and shown in the section, as well as logged.
Status still reaches watchers only on the next poll or an explicit refresh; there is no webhook intake.
justification: Receiving webhooks needs a signed listener, which the webhook area owns. The registry keeps Refresh as the one call such a component would make, so intake can be added without changing this seam.

reason: Upstream keeps the latest results in memory and loses them on restart. In Go the last snapshot of each change request is written to a derived key-value namespace when it changes, and is shown with its time until the next poll.
Upstream's tool must reject a call that has no agent. In Go the pipeline's first stage attributes every call to an agent before a body runs, so the tool body always has one.
The tools still only create, enter and leave. Listing, merging and removing a checkout or branch are not tools, and enter still reaches only the pool of the checkout the session is in.
justification: Kept on purpose: removal and merge destroy or rewrite work, and the model already has git through the shell tool under the sandbox for them. The bounded reach is the safety property of decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-6.

reason: Enter still reaches only registered worktrees inside the configured pool of the checkout the session works in, and now also only targets inside the session's write roots.
justification: Kept and tightened on purpose by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-6: a model-chosen name must not be able to move the session, and with it the write boundary, to an arbitrary directory.

reason: Leaving a worktree still keeps its branch and files, and cleanup never deletes a branch. Narrowed: a failed setup is rolled back, and what a crash or a failed removal leaves is recorded in a journal row and reported, where upstream left it unannounced.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-XFORGE-7: a branch holds commits, which are the user's work, and a checkout with uncommitted files must never be removed by the harness.

reason: Creation still fetches only the one remote branch a request names; it does not fetch other commits or missing partial-clone objects, initialise submodules, install dependencies or copy uncommitted files.
justification: Kept on purpose: an explicit pinned baseline, with no implicit network use and no repository code run during creation. Submodules and dependencies are steps the agent runs through the shell under the sandbox.

reason: Checkout still skips configured clean, smudge and process filters, so Git LFS pointers and encrypted blobs stay in their stored form.
justification: Kept on purpose: a filter is a program named by the repository's configuration, and running it during creation would execute repository code and may download. Hydration stays a step the user or agent runs deliberately.

reason: Upstream needs Node beside Git in the execution world and proceeds silently on a Git that ignores GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. In Go there is no Node helper: Git's branch lock claims the name and the file seam writes the ignore file. A version probe refuses a Git too old for the filter overrides, and one without the lazy-fetch fix when the repository has a promisor remote.

Upstream registers no grant, so a session in workspace-write cannot commit inside its worktree, and Windows ignored such grants. In Go the component holds a write-root grant for the common Git directory while the session works in the worktree, when that directory was inside the session's roots at entry, and asks for a directory session grant otherwise; the sandbox area honours every root on Windows.

The Go harness exposes enter_worktree with the same name, the arguments name and from, and the result fields path, branch, baseCommit, repositoryRoot and created. Changed: the move goes through workdir.Service.SetForCall, so a target outside the anchor is refused as workdir/outside-anchor (DH-ADR-VIEW-8); a target outside the session's current write roots is refused as worktree/outside-roots; a failed creation is rolled back.

The Go harness exposes exit_worktree with the same name, no arguments and the same result fields. Changed: it returns the session to the directory it was in when it entered, recorded as from, not to the repository's top-level directory, and the move goes through workdir.Service.SetForCall, so leaving can never widen the write boundary or move the anchor (DH-ADR-VIEW-8).

Replaced by the typed live key forge.ProvidersChanged in the notify form, carrying the family whose provider registered or withdrew; a failing listener is logged and contained, as upstream's parallel mode did.

The event announces a review write the code host accepted through the forge service. The Go forge seam is read-only: no review write, pending review or viewed mark exists, so there is nothing to announce.

Replaced by the typed live key worktree.Cleanup in the notify form, carrying the session id, the path, the journal row id and the status scheduled, retained, removed or failed. The journal row, not process memory, holds the attempt.

Replaced by the struct forgeui.Config with gitCommand, gitTimeout, grace, maxOutputBytes, readinessTimeout, maxBranches and maxUntrackedFiles at upstream's defaults, plus the new refreshThrottle (10s, upstream's fixed value). Not carried: the fifteen fields for diffs, review caches, lenses, annotations and review lists, whose features are not built; worktreePrefix is merged into worktree.Config.namePrefix so that the prefix has one owner.
Replaced by the struct forge.Config with activeInterval 30s, idleInterval 120s, maxBackoff 10m and fetchTimeout 30s, the same defaults and the same rule that maxBackoff is at least activeInterval.

Replaced by the struct github.Config with command, hosts, timeout, maxOutputBytes and maxReviewThreads at upstream's defaults. Not carried: maxCommits, maxViewedFiles and maxViewerItems, which bound reads that are not built.
Replaced by the struct bind.Config with discoveryTimeout 30s as upstream, plus the new maxScanBytes that bounds how much of a settled command's output is scanned for change-request addresses.

Replaced by the struct worktree.Config with retainOnArchive (a live field), directory, namePrefix, gitCommand, timeout, grace and maxOutputBytes at upstream's defaults. Not carried: nodeCommand, because no Node helper is started.

Replaced by the struct gitlab.Config with command, hosts, timeout, maxOutputBytes, statusBatchSize and maxConcurrentRequests at upstream's defaults. Not carried: maxReviewThreads, maxCommits and maxCachedVersionBytes, which bound review and diff reads that are not built.

ctx.forge becomes the service key forge.Key with interface forge.Service: Register and Watch as effects of the caller's fiber, Resolve, Latest, Refresh, FindByHead and Readiness. The write and review methods of upstream's service are not carried.

ctx.forgePanel is a typed remote surface for the React client. In Go the component x.forge.ui registers HTTP routes and one stream source with the API area and contributes fragments to UI regions; it offers no service, because no other component calls it.

ctx.forgeSession becomes the service key bind.Key with interface bind.Service: ChangeRequests, Watch, Track, Dismiss and DiscoverBranch. registerCommands is not carried as a runtime call: command rules are compiled-in data declared by each provider package.

ctx.worktrees becomes the service key worktree.Key with interface worktree.Service: Create, Enter, Exit and Restore as upstream, Of for the folded state, and Pending for journal rows in place of the process-local cleanupOf.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep. Checkout inspection and every worktree command run through the session's subprocess provider under its resolved sandbox mode, a refusal is never retried with less confinement, and command-local configuration disables hooks, the filesystem monitor, lazy fetch and clean and process filters. The first verdict stands; added in Go is a Git version floor, because the note records that Git older than 2.31 ignores the filter overrides.

Final verdict after reading the note: its subject is the React changes view of a large diff (memoised file sections, drawing on approach, highlighting in the drawing render). The first verdict of replaced assumed a Go changes view; this area does not build one, so there is nothing for the measures to apply to. The note's finding about document-wide CSS :has() rules is general advice for the design-system area, not a decision of this one.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep explicit creation from a pinned local commit, no fetch unless asked, no copy of uncommitted files, Git through the session's own providers, retention of branches, archive cleanup of clean unreferenced checkouts, and the rejection of automatic subagent isolation. Three points change: a failed attempt is rolled back instead of left behind, operations are journaled so a crash is recognised, and the note's refusal of any grant is replaced by retaining access to the common Git directory the session already had, because without it a session cannot commit in its own worktree.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep the host half that assembles one state per session, Git inspection in the session's execution world, polling that follows viewers, and creating the change request by asking the agent. Replace the React half with three server-rendered surfaces; replace the hold on the first message with an explicit operation before the first turn and a blocked turn on failure; drop the merge and ready actions and the changes view. The first verdict of ported overstated what is carried.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep its three rules, that bindings live in the session log with no separate store, that polled status is never logged, and that the provider reads through the host's command-line tool so credentials never enter a session's execution world; keep its rejection of a model tool. Change the mechanism: a listener writes an explicit binding event when a command settles, where the note has a projection re-read tool text, so the fold no longer depends on which rules are loaded.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep the row glyphs for a session's worktree and its most urgent change request, fed by summary folds so that unloaded sessions show them, and keep storing the last known states. Change: the note's one polling stream for every listed session is not built; rows show the stored status with its time and start no request, because the note itself records that many listed sessions mean more requests to the code host.

Final verdict after reading the note: it decides where a pull request comment kept for later is stored, and chooses the code host's pending review through the provider's writeReview. The Go forge seam is read-only and has no review threads, so no comment is drafted or written by the harness. The first verdict of ported is withdrawn.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep declarative, pure command rules owned by each provider, with the shared tokenizer and option parsing in the binding package. Drop the state version derived from the rule set and the re-registration of the projection: in Go rules are compiled in and are used only when a command settles, so no fold depends on them and no session refolds when a rule changes.

Final verdict after reading the note: the Code review page lists the user's review queue across hosts and reviews one change request without a session, through viewer lists, description reads and reads by address. It is a second review client beside the code host's own pages and needs provider reads this area does not build. The first verdict of replaced is withdrawn; the page is dropped by decision.
